absent: Semantics and flag modifiers of the table construction helpers and the in-memory layout of register-to-feature table rows.
Numeric bit positions and masks for the named control fields and reserved-bit constants.
Definitions and detection logic for the architecture feature predicates referenced by the tables.
Treatment of enhanced host mode transitions and how default-on versus gated behaviour is enforced.
Implementation of the host-ownership predicate and the effects of refreshing debug controls.
Storage and concurrency rules for host-wide trace flags and staged trace configuration.
Full evaluation algorithm that consumes single, combination and callback trap groups to decide forwarding.
Bodies and triggering conditions of the complex trap callbacks for counters, authentication and nested virtualization.
Ownership and lifetime rules for vCPU debug state across put and load.
Error handling and return contracts for the debug and trace entry points beyond what the fragments show.

findings.text: TCR2 capability gating is expressed as a table where each row associates a set of translation controls with the architecture extension that permits them, with several rows additionally conditioned on enhanced host mode, and the table closes with masks that force reserved positions to fixed values.

EL1 system control gating is expressed as a table where most control fields each require a distinct architecture extension, a large collection of basic controls shares a common baseline requirement, and reserved masks pin undefined positions.

EL2 system control gating mirrors the EL1 controls but many rows add a requirement for enhanced host mode and some rows change their default treatment according to that mode, with a baseline group and reserved masks closing the table.

EL2 debug control gating is expressed as a table where each trap or enable field requires its matching debug, counting, sampling or trace extension, including grouped counter fields and a baseline group, closed by reserved masks.

Stage-2 translation control gating is expressed as a table where tagging, granule, partitioning, fault and permission fields each require their matching extension, access handling consults identifier register predicates, and a baseline group plus reserved masks complete the table.

Interrupt virtualization fine-grain trap controls for read, write and instruction classes are each gated as a group by one common extension, so all listed trap bits in each table share the same requirement.
A trap descriptor logically holds a selector for its governing control register, a forwarding policy, an expected value used for comparison, and a mask selecting the significant bits.

Trap disposition uses zero for local handling, one low bit to request read forwarding, another low bit to request write forwarding with their combination meaning both directions, and a separate higher bit to indicate effect while the host runs in unprivileged mode.

Coarse trap groups are partitioned into three ranges separated by sentinels: an initial range of single-control groups, a middle range where each group combines several single controls, and a final range evaluated by callbacks, with a leading reserved value and trailing count.

Each single-control group is bound to one governing control register with a masked expectation and an attached forwarding direction; most groups match when the governed bit is set while a few match when it is clear, and forwarding varies among read-only, write-only and bidirectional.

Combination groups are defined as short terminated lists of single-control groups that are evaluated together, capturing interactions where two or three governing controls jointly determine forwarding.
Groups in the complex range delegate their forwarding decision to a per-group callback that inspects vCPU state and returns a trap disposition.
Guest ownership of debug registers can be requested for a vCPU; the request has no effect while host ownership is reported and otherwise records guest ownership and refreshes debug configuration.

Debug register ownership distinguishes host-owned and guest-owned states, with a guarded transition into guest-owned state that leaves host-owned state unchanged when the guard reports host ownership.
OS lock requests update the guest-visible lock status view and are made effective by reloading the vCPU on its current physical CPU.
Reloading the vCPU to make an OS lock change effective is performed with preemption disabled across the put and load pair.

Trace buffer extension access must not be performed in protected mode, before subsystem initialization, when the caller passes a suppressing condition, or in a context where preemption is allowed, with the last case additionally producing a one-time diagnostic.
Host-wide trace buffer enablement can only be set or cleared when mode and context checks permit; virtualized host extension state participates in that permission check.

EL1 trace configuration is applied directly to the aliased register when virtualized host extensions are present and otherwise is staged in host storage with a flag recording whether staged state diverges from current hardware state; protected, uninitialized or preemptible contexts suppress any update.
